Condition : 1 - The permission hereby granted shall be for a limited period, being the period of 153 weeks from the date of commencement of the approved development. Written notice that works have formally commenced shall be provided by email to the Local Planning Authority within 7 days of the commencement of works. The use hereby permitted shall cease and/or any approved structures shall be removed and the land restored to its former use as a playing field, as set out within Condition 2 of this decision. 
Reason: The proposal is not considered suitable as a permanent form of development to safeguard neighbours' living conditions and the character and appearance of the area. 
Condition : 2 - Prior to commencement of the approved development, a scheme for the removal of the temporary classroom building and the reinstatement of the playing field should be submitted and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority after consultation with Sport England. 
The scheme must be in accordance with Sport England guidance "Natural Turf for Sport" and contain measures for replacing the existing artificial cricket wicket.
The temporary classroom building must be removed from the site within 3 months of the first occupation of the permanent new school buildings in accordance with the approved scheme.
Within three months of or in the first planting season following the removal of the temporary classroom building the affected playing field must be reinstated in accordance with the approved scheme.
Reason: To ensure the site is restored to a condition fit for purpose and to accord with Local Plan policy GB3.
Condition : 3 - The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans and specifications: 
[SRP1143-ONE-ZZ-XX-D-L-0018-P02, SRP1143-ONE-ZZ-XX-D-L-0019-P01, SRP1143-ONE-ZZ-XX-D-L-0017-P06, SRP1143-ONE-ZZ-XX-D-L-0015-P03, 37817-PML-B1-ZZ-DR-A-0060 P2, 37817-PML-B1-ZZ-DR-A-0005 P0,  7817-PML-B1-ZZ-DR-A-0001 P13, 37817-PML-B1-RF-DR-A-0004 P0, 37817-PML-B1-XX-M2-A-Sk100 V2, 37817-PML-B1-ZZ-DR-A-0002 P2- All received 31/03/2025; 
Air Quality Screening Assessment (doc ref- GM13797 V1.0, dtd- 06/03/2025, by Wardell Armstrong), Archaeological Desk-Based Assessment (doc ref: 240116-DBA-2024419-Issue2, by ASE), Construction Environmental Management Plan (Issue- P3, dtd- 13/03/2025, by B+K), Sunlight & Daylight Impact (doc ref- 288774-29a, dtd- 21/01/2025, by Arup),   
Ecological Impact Assessment (doc ref- SRP1143-DSI-XX-XX-T-O-0002-P02, dtd September 2024, prepared by Delta Simons), 
Biodiversity Net Gain Assessment (doc ref- SRP1143-DSI-XX-XX-T-O-0002-P01, by Delta Simons), Biodiversity Net Gain Metric , Energy Statement (Rev 01, dtd March 2025, by Premier Modular), Flood Risk and Drainage Assessment (proj no.- JAG/MS/JF/50353-Rp002, dtd 14/01/2025, by Alan Wood & Partners), Drainage Assessment Form, Phase 1 Desk Study (doc ref- GM12495, report 001, V1.0, dtd October 2022, by Wardell Armstrong), Rapid Health Impact Assessment (doc ref- 5675LO/R002, dtd 24/03/2025, by DPP), External Lighting Layout Temp Building (SRP1143-CDL-XX-XX-D-E-9602, by Cundall), Temporary Building Lighting Impact Assessment (RAWL Temporary Building � Lighting Impact Assessment Supplementary Note, by Cundall), Noise Impact Assessment (SRP1143-BHE-XX-XX-T-J-0003, dtd 14/03/2025, by Buro Happold), Phasing Plans (SPR1143-BNK-XX-XX-DR-X-1010(P01), SPR1143-BNK-XX-XX-DR-X-1011(P01), SPR1143-BNK-XX-XX-DR-X-1020(P01), SPR1143-BNK-XX-XX-DR-X-1030(P01), SPR1143-BNK-XX-XX-DR-X-1031(P01), , SPR1143-BNK-XX-XX-DR-X-1040(P01)), Letter of Comfort from Principal regarding playing fie
Condition : 4 - The hereby approved development must be carried out in accordance with the approved Energy Statement. 
Reason: To ensure that the development makes the fullest contribution to minimising carbon dioxide emissions
Condition : 5 - a)	Prior to commencement of groundworks (excluding site investigations and demolition), the applicant must submit a final detailed drainage design including drawings and supporting calculations [and updated Drainage Assessment Form] to the Lead Local Flood Authority for review and approval, aligned with the submitted Flood Risk and Drainage Assessment and associated drawings. It must be confirmed that the ground conditions are suitable for infiltration, or amendments made to the strategy should a connection to the surface water sewer be required, in line with policy requirements. The proposed storage volume should be made clear and the calculations updated to use FEH22 rainfall data. A detailed management plan confirming routine maintenance tasks for all drainage components must also be submitted to demonstrate how the drainage system is to be maintained during the lifetime of the development. A maintenance owner should be provided.
b)	No building hereby permitted shall be occupied until evidence (photographs and installation contracts) is submitted to demonstrate that the sustainable drainage scheme for the site has been completed in accordance with the submitted details. The sustainable drainage scheme shall be managed and maintained during the lifetime of the development in accordance with the agreed management and maintenance plan for all of the proposed drainage components.
Reason: To prevent the risk of flooding to and from the site in accordance with relevant policy requirements including but not limited to London Plan Policy SI 13, its associated Sustainable Design and Construction SPG, the Non-Statutory Technical Standards for Sustainable Drainage Systems and Hounslow Council's Local Plan Policy EQ3.
Condition : 6 - The development shall not be occupied until confirmation is provided that either:
1. All necessary upgrades to the foul water network to accommodate additional flows from the development have been completed; or
2. A phasing plan for development and infrastructure, agreed with Thames Water and the Local Planning Authority, is in place. Where such a plan exists, no occupation shall occur other than in accordance with the approved phasing schedule.

Reason: Network reinforcement is likely to be required to support the proposed development. These upgrades are essential to avoid the risk of sewer flooding and pollution incidents.
Condition : 7 - Prior to commencement of any development, an updated detailed air quality assessment assessing operational and construction phase impacts must be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority. The updated detailed air quality assessment must address all London Borough of Hounslow comments made on the previous assessment.  The updated air quality assessment must be carried out in accordance with all new and updated relevant policy and guidance documents at the time of writing, as well as using the most up to date Defra tools (such as EFT and NOX to NO2) and 2021 reference year background maps. 
Reason: In the interests of air quality and to protect neighbours' living conditions and the wider local environment. 
Condition : 8 - a)	Prior to erection of the buildings on site a scheme of sound insulation shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority as necessary to achieve the relevant internal noise level criteria as specified in 'Building bulletin 93 - Acoustic design of schools: performance standards' (BB93). 
b)	Prior to first occupation of any building used for teaching or learning, validation testing should be carried out, and results approved by the Local Planning Authority, to demonstrate that suitable internal ambient noise levels in accordance with BB93 have been achieved on site. The testing should be carried out in accordance with the latest version of 'ANC Good Practice Guide - Acoustic Testing of Schools'.
Any remedial measures to achieve the BB93 internal noise level criteria should be installed prior to the validation testing and thereafter be permanently retained whilst the building is used for teaching or learning purposes on site.
Reason: In the interests proving acceptable internal conditions for the occupants of the development.
Condition : 9 - Based upon guidance contained within BS 5228:2009 + A1:2014: Noise, Noise levels from construction works at nearby existing and proposed residential receptors shall not exceed the following construction noise criteria:
- Daytime works will not exceed 75 dB LAeq,T at the worst-affected residential property during the following time periods:
�	Monday to Friday (08:00 � 18:00 hours) 	 
�	Saturday (08:00 to 13:00 hours)
Works outside of the standard hours will be subject to prior agreement and prior notice will be provided to the London Borough of Hounslow.
Reason: In order to protect neighbours' living conditions.
Condition : 10 - The cumulative noise from any fixed external plant associated with the scheme should not exceed levels more than 10 dB below representative background (LA90) levels at free field locations representing facades of nearby existing and proposed dwellings, over any period that the plant is operational. Noise levels should be assessed by measurement or calculation based on the guidance presented within BS4142: 2014+A1:2019 or subsequent versions of this guidance.
Reason: In order to ensure that occupants of the development and its neighbours are not exposed to unreasonable levels of fixed plant noise.
Condition : 11 - No development shall take place until a detailed Construction Logistics Plan (CLP), written in accordance with current TfL guidance, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The CLP shall include:
(a)	a site plan (showing the elements set out below);
(b)	confirmation that a pre-start record of site conditions on the adjoining public highway will be undertaken with Hounslow Highways and a commitment to repair any damage caused;
(c)	provision for the parking of vehicles of site operatives and visitors;
(d)	provisions for loading, unloading and storage of plant and materials within the site;
(e)	details of access to the site, including means to control and manage access and egress of vehicles to and from the site for the duration of construction including phasing arrangements;
(f)	details of vehicle routeing from the site to the wider strategic road network;
(g)	the erection and maintenance of security hoarding including decorative displays and facilities for public viewing, where appropriate;
(h)	provision of wheel washing facilities at the site exit and a commitment to sweep adjacent roads when required and at the request of the Council;
(i)	a scheme for recycling/disposing of waste resulting from demolition and construction works; 
(j)	measures to ensure the safety of all users of the public highway especially cyclists and pedestrians in the vicinity of the site and especially at the access;
(k)	commitment to liaise with other contractors in the vicinity of the site to maximise the potential for consolidation and to minimise traffic impacts;
(l)	avoidance of peak hours for deliveries and details of a booking system to avoid vehicles waiting on the public highway;
(m)	all necessary traffic orders and other permissions required to allow safe access to the site to be secured and implemented prior to commencement of construction;
(n)	details of the construction programme and a schedule of traffic movements;
(o)	the us
Condition : 12 - Three months prior to the commencement of the temporary use, a School Access Strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Strategy shall set out how safe and efficient access will be provided for all users of the site during the temporary use.  The Strategy shall include, but not be limited to:
a)	A breakdown of number of student crossing movements on Letchworth Avenue, including estimated students and timings
b)	Details of access controls and supervision measures during school hours, particularly at arrival, departure and lunchtime periods, and 
c)	Location and design of internal circulation routes, access points, crossing facilities, gates, signage, and on-site supervision;
d)	Details of any temporary or phased access arrangements and how safety will be managed throughout the duration of the temporary use.
e)	Details of delivery, servicing and refuse management strategy for the development for the duration of the temporary use.
The approved measures shall be implemented in full prior to the temporary use commencing and maintained throughout the duration of that use.
Reason: In order to ensure highway safety is maintained and preserved, and minimal disruption of traffic in the locality.
Condition : 13 - Before the development hereby permitted is first occupied or brought into use, a Parking Management Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Plan shall include the following:
a)	details of parking allocations for various users for the approved development and how this will be operated and enforced
b)	details of measures proposed to restrict parking to designated bays only and prohibit parking on the access road
c)	details of the operation of any gates or barriers
d)	measures to ensure that all staff members are informed of the Parking Management Plan 
The parking areas and access road(s) shall thereafter be managed during the lifetime of the development in compliance with the approved Parking Management Plan, unless the prior written approval of the local planning authority is obtained to secure any variation.
Reason: In order to promote sustainable modes of transport, to protect neighbours' living conditions and to ensure minimal disruption of traffic in the locality.
Condition : 14 - No development above ground level (except any demolition, site clearance, ground investigation and remediation work) shall take place until details of the amended vehicular (emergency vehicles only) and pedestrian access to the site, alongside combined Road Safety Audit (Stage 1/2), shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. No part of the development shall be brought into use until the new means of access has been sited, laid out and constructed in accordance with the approved details, and retained as such thereafter.
Reason: In order to ensure safe access and highway safety.
Condition : 15 - Prior to the first use or occupation of the development full details (including manufacturers' specifications) of secure covered cycle parking facilities that accord with the West London Cycle Parking Guidance (or any guidance that supersedes this) for the occupants of, and visitors to, the development shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved facilities shall be fully implemented and made available for use before the development is first occupied or brought into use, The approved facilities shall be thereafter retained for use during the lifetime of the development without obstruction.
Reason: In order to support sustainable transport objectives.
Condition : 16 - All refuse and recycling bins, delivery cages, trolleys or any other items linked to deliveries and collection in association with the approved development are to be stored within the building(s) at all times and only brought out onto the public highway when deliveries are being made or refuse collected.
Reason: To protect the quality of the local environment and to prevent obstruction and inconvenience to users of the public highway
Condition : 17 - No development shall take place until an Ecological Management Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.
The Ecological Management Plan shall incorporate:
a)	 measures, including toolbox talks, to protect breeding birds, nests and eggs from mortality/damage, injury and disturbance, including avoidance by timing and/or appropriate supervision.
b)	species surveys within and around the site to demonstrate ecological enhancements 
c)	additional detail on location and type of bird/bat boxes, insect hotels, maintenance and a commitment that any data collected is to be shared with the Council;
d)	details of ecological enhancement and urban greening factor, including how the urban greening factor is to be delivered and achieved on site;
e)	an ecological lighting plan;
f)	details of how the enhancement measures will be monitored, managed and maintained, including the long- term design objectives, management responsibilities and maintenance schedules;
The development shall then be carried out in accordance with the approved details.
Reason: In the interests of nature conservation.
Condition : 18 - Notwithstanding the details submitted, no development shall take place (including vegetation clearance, demolition, and ground works) until a Construction Environment Management Plan (CEMP) has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the local planning authority. The Plan shall include: 
a)	Identification of stages of works, details of working hours
b)	Risk assessment and mitigation measures for construction traffic, noise and vibration, dust and air pollutants, land contamination, ecology and ground water. 
c)	Setting up of site- protective fences, exclusion barriers and warning signs
d)	Details of the ecological clerk of works or responsible person and lines of communication, 
e)	Watching brief for bats, birds, reptiles and amphibians including details of the pre-development checks, and, identified on maps where applicable, measures to mitigate the impacts of construction activities on wildlife, construction lighting plan, and details of any licensing requirement
f)	Protocol for non-native invasive species, unexpected fauna if encountered on site
g)	Communication with the neighbouring residents in order to safeguard the amenities of the adjoining premises and the area in general.

The approved CEMP should be followed and implemented throughout the construction period in accordance with the approved details.
Reason: In order to ensure the protection of wildlife and supporting habitat and secure opportunities for the enhancement of the nature conservation value of the site.
Condition : 19 - Notwithstanding any details included in the submitted plans, no development above ground level (except any demolition, site clearance, ground investigation and remediation work) shall take place until details of both hard and soft landscape works have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. These details shall include: 
a)	a statement setting out the design objectives and how these will be delivered;  
b)	access and circulation areas, materials, means of enclosure/boundary treatment(s) and retaining structures; 
c)	minor artefacts and structures (e.g. furniture, play equipment, refuse or other storage units, signs, lighting, CCTV,  etc.); 
d)	retained historic or other landscape features and proposals for restoration, where relevant; 
e)	where applicable, planting plans, written specifications (including cultivation and other operations associated with plant and grass establishment); schedules of plants, noting species, plant sizes and proposed numbers and densities where appropriate; and
f)	an implementation programme (including phasing of work where relevant).
The landscaping works shall comply with the requirements specified in BS 3936 (1992) 'Specification of Nursery Stock Part 1 Trees and Shrubs', and in BS 4428 (1989) 'Recommendations for General Landscape Operations', and shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details before the development hereby permitted is first occupied or brought into use, or such other date(s) as may be specified in the agreed implementation programme.
The trees that are specified on drawings SRP1143-HAY-XX-XX-D-O-0001-P01 and SRP1143-HAY-XX-XX-D-O-0002-P01 hereby approved to be retained and shall be protected before commencement of any works on site and throughout the course of the development by methods that conform to the best practice guidance contained in British Standard BS5837: 2012 or any guidance that shall have superseded it.

Condition : 20 - Prior to the first commencement of the hereby approved development, a Biodiversity Gain Plan shall  be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, the Plan shall include; (a) information about the steps taken or to be taken to minimise the adverse effect of the development on the biodiversity of the onsite habitat and any other habitat, (b) the pre-development biodiversity value of the onsite habitat, (c) the post-development biodiversity value of the onsite habitat, (d) any registered offsite biodiversity gain allocated to the development and the biodiversity value of that gain in relation to the development, (e) any biodiversity credits purchased for the development, and (f) such other matters as the Secretary of State may by regulations specify. The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved Plan prior to the first occupation of the development. Any habitats created or enhanced on-site and off-site in accordance with the Biodiversity Gain Plan must be maintained thereafter for a minimum of 30 years. 
Reason. In the interests of improving Biodiversity and in accordance with The Town and Country Planning Act 1990, Section 90A, Schedule 7A.
Condition : 21 - If the Biodiversity Gain Plan identifies any on-site provision of habitats, notwithstanding the submitted details, no above ground works, excluding demolition, remediation and groundworks, shall take place until a habitat management plan in accordance with the approved Biodiversity Gain Plan must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. 
The habitat management plan shall include:
a)	Prescription for management actions.
b)	Preparation of the work schedule (including an annual work Plan for over 30-year period and who will carry out the jobs mentioned in the management plans).
c)	Details of the body or organisation responsible for implementation of the plan.
d)	Time frame for reviewing the plan.
e)	Details of the management plans and its communication to the occupiers of the development.
Reason: In the interests of improving Biodiversity and in accordance with The Town and Country Planning Act 1990, Section 90A, Schedule 7A.
